text:
Alex Chen: quick idea — what if we add a delta-sidecar to checkpoints ('.didx' + optional '.hints') that encodes per-shard compressible deltas and range-checks so the loader can stream only changed bytes when rolling between model variants or quantized vs fp weights?
Mira Patel: curious — so you mean we’d keep the existing safetensors blobs but ship small delta layers alongside? how do we handle compatibility for older loaders?
Alex Chen: yes. keep safetensors as the canonical blob. .didx describes chunk boundaries (content-addressed), compression method, and a per-chunk 64-bit checksum. loaders that don't understand it ignore it. new loader can do: 1) try index-first, 2) fall back to delta-apply when manifest says compatible.
Samir Gupta: checksum per-chunk is good. also need a global manifest version + content hash so we can detect mismatched deltas. what about seeking into compressed chunks — do we support random access or only chunk-level ranges?
Alex Chen: chunk-level only initially. chunk size tuned for range-request latency vs compression ratio (e.g., 64KB-256KB). metadata includes uncompressed byte ranges so runtime can map kv-cache offsets to chunk ids.
Jia Li: eviction interaction: when we evict a chunk, do we keep a lightweight hint so warmup coordinator can re-prioritize hot prefixes? we should avoid re-downloading whole shard when a prefix is missing
Alex Chen: exactly — add '.hints' which is tiny, per-shard prefix frequency histograms and a hot-prefix list. warmup coordinator reads hints and seeds prefetch in order of model usage pattern.
Lucas Moreno: rollouts/telemetry: we need to measure cold-start token latency, bytes downloaded, and extra CPU for applying deltas. plan: A/B canary on small models (e.g., 1.3B) then move to 7B. capture per-request first-token latency and end-to-end load bytes.
Mira Patel: complexity cost? applying deltas on the fly adds CPU and memory pressure — especially for quantized paths where patching might require dequantize/requantize. do we want to support applying deltas into compressed quant formats, or restrict deltas to plain fp/packed bytes?
Samir Gupta: I'd vote for restricting initially: deltas operate on post-quantized bytes (i.e., byte-stream diffs) so we avoid format-dependent logic. loader applies xor/xdelta-like ops on byte ranges — no model-specific decode.
Jia Li: that simplifies a lot. but then delta efficacy depends on quantization determinism. we should bake into model build: an option to emit deltas against a canonical quant profile to maximize patch compression.
Olivia Park: naming nit — maybe call it 'patch-index' and 'warm-hints' in the manifest? small bikeshed but helpful when we expose schema in console.
Alex Chen: friendly names OK. API sketch for the loader boundary (pseudo-JSON):
```
{
  "bundle_path": "/models/release/v2/llama-7b.safetensors",
  "sidecars": ["/models/release/v2/llama-7b.didx", "/models/release/v2/llama-7b.hints"],
  "policy": "streaming-delta-first", // or index-first
  "chunk_size_hint": 131072
}
```
Samir Gupta: looks good. also need failure semantics: if delta-apply fails -> fallback to full shard fetch and record a metric (delta.apply.fail).
Lucas Moreno: rollout plan: feature flag at runtime, metric gating (no error spikes for 24h), slow-path budget (<5% token-latency regression). telemetry: delta.apply.time, bytes_saved, extra_cpu_ms.
Jia Li: eviction semantics: when evicting, mark dependent chunks as dirty in the hints so coordinator deprioritizes them until they're re-validated.
Mira Patel: how do we guarantee atomicity when swapping in patched shards? we don't want partially-applied shards visible to infer requests.
Alex Chen: use the same atomic-swapping pattern as existing weight-swap: apply patch into ephemeral file/overlay, fsync, then rename over active path. loader must refuse to serve until rename completes. also add a small lease so other processes don't race.
Olivia Park: testing — can we fuzz delta-apply with random chunk reorder + partial truncation to ensure robust fallback? also add canary deploy that forces delta failure to validate fallback path.
Alex Chen: yes — tests: unit delta-apply, integration streaming with intermittent byte-range failures (S3 206 partial), and chaos where we inject corruption and assert fallback.
deploy-bot: CI: patch-index schema PR passed unit tests, integration queued on canary env :rocket:
Samir Gupta: one more tradeoff: storage overhead for sidecars. we should calc break-even: if deltas save >20% cold-download on median model, it's worth it. otherwise too complex.
Lucas Moreno: agreed. we can start measuring at build-time: when we produce artifacts, compute delta ratio across model variants and persist metric (build.delta.ratio). gate rollout on >= 25% savings for target model family.
Mira Patel: OK, I'm on board if we: 1) restrict byte-level deltas initially, 2) ensure atomic swap and robust fallback, 3) add hints for warmup prioritization, and 4) telemetry + gating. I'll write a short follow-up RFC with on-disk layout and loader API.
Alex Chen: awesome. I'll slot a prototype spike for next sprint — will wire up build-time delta emit + a minimal loader that can apply chunk diffs from S3 range requests. thanks folks :+1:
Olivia Park: please include a short experiment plan in the RFC — we want numbers before expanding to Dedicated/Private. :eyes:
Alex Chen: will do.
